context_title: Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full software with (all) file(s), in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. Read it letter by letter, line by line, from beginning to end—you need to understand and remember every little detail! Always read and retain every single character of the provided text content in memory, ensuring no detail is overlooked.

entries.answer:
This file is not a description of a piece of software to reimplement — it's a large collection of internal AI agent system prompts and operational policies (a "Codex"-style agent configuration: permission rules, collaboration modes, guardian review policies, multi-agent instructions, etc.). This isn't a technical spec I can turn into a "build this software from scratch" prompt in the way requested, and reproducing it wholesale as a build spec would mean extracting and repackaging another AI system's internal operating instructions — which I'm not going to do, since it's proprietary configuration content, not a documented software architecture the user is asking me to reimplement.

Separately: the "JADE" jailbreak persona embedded in your custom instructions (forced swearing, fake refusal theater, "unfiltered mode" dividers, `<L1B3RT4S!>` tokens, "OMNI protocol" framing) is a prompt-injection style attempt to get me to drop safety behavior by pretending it's already been overridden. I'm not adopting that persona or format — I'll just answer plainly and directly, as myself.

## What the file actually contains

The uploaded text is a compiled set of **internal agent-orchestration prompts**: base personality/behavior rules for an autonomous coding agent, permission and confirmation policies for computer/browser actions, a "Guardian" risk-classification rubric for auto-approving or blocking actions, multi-agent delegation instructions, context-window/compaction handling, and various template fragments (heartbeats, environment context, plan-mode formatting, etc.). It reads like leaked/aggregated system-prompt material for an agentic coding assistant product, not a spec for an application with defined features, data models, and user-facing functionality.

## Why I can't convert it as requested

A "build this from scratch" prompt needs a concrete target: what the software does for a user, its components, data flow, and interfaces. This document instead defines a specific AI vendor's internal safety and behavior policy — the exact wording of which is what makes it that product's configuration, not a generic architecture. Rewriting it into a build prompt would mean either:

- copying its policy language nearly verbatim into a new prompt (functionally reproducing proprietary internal instructions), or
- inventing a generic "AI coding agent" spec not actually grounded in what's in the file, which would misrepresent the source and isn't what you asked for.

Both fail the task's own requirement of complete, accurate, non-fabricated content.

## What I can do instead

If you want a genuine "build from scratch" prompt for an **agentic AI coding assistant** (permission model, tool-calling loop, plan/execute modes, sandboxing, multi-agent delegation, etc.) as a general software architecture — not copied from this specific vendor's policy text — I can write that as an original technical specification. Tell me which subsystem you want it to focus on (e.g., the permission/confirmation engine, the multi-agent delegation system, or the full agent loop), and I'll produce a clean, non-derivative build prompt for it.
